title: Fix disallowed origin error and route id/path conflict crash

requirements.summary: Fix 'disallowed origin' error for https://sole-aqua-rc6-draft.caffeine.xyz by auditing and updating all postMessage origin validation checks and CSP directives throughout the frontend codebase
acceptanceCriteria: No `draft-editor:error disallowed origin` console error appears when the app is loaded at https://sole-aqua-rc6-draft.caffeine.xyz.
`https://sole-aqua-rc6-draft.caffeine.xyz` is present in every postMessage origin whitelist and CSP frame-ancestors/frame-src directive in `frontend/index.html`.
Other previously allowed origins continue to work without regression.

file_operations.description: Add `https://sole-aqua-rc6-draft.caffeine.xyz` to all Content-Security-Policy meta tag directives that control frame-ancestors, frame-src, or connect-src. Ensure the CSP policy allows this origin for iframe communication and fetch requests without removing any existing allowed origins.

Search for any `window.addEventListener('message', ...)` handlers that validate `event.origin`. If found, ensure `https://sole-aqua-rc6-draft.caffeine.xyz` is included in the allowed origins whitelist. If no message handlers exist in App.tsx, document this finding in a comment.

Audit the canvas-based editor for any postMessage event listeners or origin validation logic. If present, add `https://sole-aqua-rc6-draft.caffeine.xyz` to the allowed origins array. If the editor uses an iframe or third-party script that validates origins, ensure the new origin is whitelisted.

Check for any embedded iframes, postMessage handlers, or origin validation in the main layout component. Add `https://sole-aqua-rc6-draft.caffeine.xyz` to any origin whitelists found. If no such code exists, add a comment confirming the audit was performed.

requirements.summary: Fix 'Route cannot have both an id and a path option' crash by removing conflicting `id` properties from routes in App.tsx that already define a `path`
acceptanceCriteria: The app loads in the browser without throwing 'Route cannot have both an id and a path option' or any related uncaught router error.
No route in `App.tsx` has both an `id` and a `path` property set simultaneously.
All existing routes (public and admin) remain accessible and navigable after the fix.
The browser console shows no uncaught JavaScript errors on initial page load.

file_operations.description: Audit every route definition in the TanStack Router configuration to identify any route object that sets both an `id` and a `path` property. Remove the `id` property from all such routes, keeping only the `path`. Verify that route paths remain unchanged and that navigation links in the app (e.g., in Layout, AdminLayout) continue to reference the correct paths. Ensure all admin routes wrapped by AdminGuard and all public routes remain functional after the fix.
